articles.title: Liposomal bupivacaine surgical site injection for decrease of narcotic use in hip fractures: a pilot multicenter randomized trial.
articles.authors: Matuszewski PE, Jo J, Aneja A, Diwan A, Kraus MT, Moghadamian ES, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged over 55 years with isolated fragility hip fractures undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Primary: morphine milliequivalents at 24, 48 and 72 hours after surgery. Secondary: pain scores, confusion assessment, delirium episodes and surgical or medical complications.
articles.take_home: Liposomal bupivacaine injected at the surgical site did not reduce the amount of painkillers needed after hip fracture surgery compared to placebo, nor did it reduce pain scores or confusion in older patients. The authors concluded that a larger trial is unlikely to be worthwhile given the expense and complexity of the treatment.

articles.title: Vertically Unstable Pelvic Ring Injuries: Impact of Multilevel and Transsacral Fixation Strategy on Failure Rate.
articles.authors: Luther L, Maxson R, Moreno-Diaz AF, Chenard SW, Tatman LM, Mitchell PM
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over with vertically unstable pelvic ring injuries treated with percutaneous pelvic fixation
articles.sample_size: 67 patients (38 with multilevel and transsacral fixation, 29 with single-level or sacroiliac screw-only fixation)
articles.outcomes: Treatment failure (radiographic displacement of 10 mm or more), revision surgery rates
articles.take_home: Pelvic fractures treated with fixation at multiple sacral levels including transsacral screws had a much lower failure rate (2.6%) compared to single-level fixation (48.3%). Using this more comprehensive fixation approach also reduced the need for further surgery.

articles.title: Postoperative subclinical nerve injury after closed reduction and percutaneous pinning of paediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a prospective Electromyographic study.
articles.authors: Kandemir I, Igrek S, Inan RA, Bayhan M, Zihni H, Eceviz E
articles.population: Children aged 1-12 years with severe upper arm bone fractures (Gartland type III and IV supracondylar humerus fractures) treated with closed reduction and percutaneous pinning
articles.sample_size: 73 patients (31 females, 42 males; mean age 5.68 years)
articles.outcomes: Electromyography-detected nerve injury (axonal damage) in median, ulnar, or radial nerves within one week after pin removal at one month post-surgery; identification of surgical and radiographic risk factors for ulnar nerve injury
articles.take_home: Nearly one quarter of children showed nerve damage on electrical testing despite normal clinical examinations after surgery. Placing the medial pin too far back and down, and longer operating times, were associated with increased risk of ulnar nerve injury that may not be immediately obvious to clinicians.

articles.title: Outcomes of Aseptic, Septic, and Occult Infected Index Nonunion Repair: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Rossbach K, Mau M, Marchand L, Higgins T, Rothberg D, Haller J
articles.population: Skeletally mature patients with nonunion fractures and inflammatory markers at time of surgery
articles.outcomes: Successful bone union after surgery without need for further operations; postoperative infection rates
articles.take_home: Bones that fail to heal due to hidden infection did almost as well after surgery as those without infection (79% versus 73% healed successfully), but bones with confirmed active infection had worse results (50% healed successfully and 35% developed new infections afterwards).

articles.title: Plate Fixation with and without Suture Endobutton Augmentation of the CoracoClavicular Ligament in displaced Lateral Clavicle Fractures: A Comparative Outcome Study.
articles.authors: Katzir A, Klinger CE, Bilodeau R, Bhadouriya RS, Schlauch A, Kantor AH, et al.
articles.population: Adults with displaced lateral clavicle fractures
articles.outcomes: Bone union, coracoclavicular distance stability, infection rates, hardware removal rates, arm function (QuickDASH score), and pain scores
articles.take_home: Plate fixation with added suture Endobutton achieved bone healing in all patients compared to 93% without it, though this difference was not statistically significant. Both groups had similar long-term stability, low pain, and good arm function at an average of three years follow-up.

articles.title: Quantifying the effects of eccentrically drilled distal interlock screws in cadaveric tibias.
articles.authors: McDonald C, Atkinson C, Ni A, Papanikolaou K, Ullah R, Hand TL
articles.population: Human cadaveric tibias with simulated distal fractures
articles.outcomes: Angular displacement (coronal and sagittal angulation) and axial length changes following eccentric distal interlocking screw placement
articles.take_home: When surgeons drill off-centre during distal screw placement in tibial nailing, it can cause measurable misalignment of about 6 degrees and shifts of up to 4mm. Surgeons should aim for precise drilling technique to avoid these alignment problems after surgery.

articles.title: Abdominal trauma in the Sudan conflict: A multicentre analysis of injury patterns, surgical management, and mortality predictors (May 2023 - January 2025).
articles.authors: Khair MM, Elsharif SAM, Mohamed AMI, Hamza AAA, Abass AOA, Dowa AE, et al.
articles.population: Patients with abdominal trauma from armed conflict in Sudan, mostly civilians from urban areas
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality 6.7% (among those surviving first 24 hours), wound infection 12.6%, sepsis 5.5%, shock 5.1%
articles.take_home: Most abdominal injuries in the Sudan conflict were from bullets or shells affecting the small bowel and colon. Among patients who survived the first day in hospital, most lived, but early shock and severe injuries increased death risk.

articles.title: Fracture laterality as an independent prognostic factor for clinical outcomes after hip fracture surgery : an analysis of 72,008 patients.
articles.authors: Takegami Y, Imaizumi T, Sato K, Osawa Y, Funahashi H, Imagama S
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using administrative database
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary surgery for hip fracture in Japan between 2015 and 2023
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcome: impaired independence in activities of daily living at discharge (Barthel index score less than 60)
articles.take_home: Right-sided hip fractures were associated with worse independence in daily activities after discharge compared to left-sided fractures. Right-sided fractures were also linked to higher death rates in hospital among patients with multiple other health conditions.

articles.title: Wear performance of metal and ceramic long-neck femoral head taper connections: an experimental ex vivo study.
articles.authors: Ribeiro de Sousa M, Neuvonen P, Saikko V
articles.population: Femoral head taper connections with metal (CoCr) and ceramic (ZTA) heads of 36 mm diameter
articles.outcomes: Wear performance measured by optical and scanning electron microscopy, metal release (Ti and Co) by mass spectrometry, and head disassembly forces
articles.take_home: Long and extra-long neck femoral heads showed increased wear compared with medium neck heads, with metal heads being more affected than ceramic heads. Although one neck fracture occurred during testing, the findings suggest that neck length choice may influence how quickly hip replacement components wear.

articles.title: Single versus dual antibiotic-loaded bone cement in hip fracture arthroplasty: a cohort study of 56,434 hip arthroplasties from the Dutch Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Yoon SJ, Van Marle L, Van Steenbergen LN, Bos PK, Jutte PC, Wouthuyzen-Bakker M, et al.
articles.study_type: Cohort study using national register data
articles.population: Patients aged any age treated with cemented hip arthroplasty for proximal femoral fracture
articles.sample_size: 56,434 hip arthroplasties (1,651 with dual antibiotic cement, remainder with single antibiotic cement)
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, revision for infection, and mortality within 1 year and beyond
articles.take_home: Using dual antibiotic-loaded bone cement in hip fracture surgery did not reduce the need for repeat surgery compared with single antibiotic cement, and was actually associated with a slightly higher risk of revision for infection and death.

articles.title: Prehospital national early warning score outperforms shock index in predicting mortality and resource utilisation in adult trauma: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Tolich A, Dicker B, Howie G, Todd VF
articles.population: Adult trauma patients in prehospital settings
articles.sample_size: 22 studies included; individual study sizes ranged from 184 to 1,439,221 patients
articles.outcomes: Mortality prediction, transfusion requirement, critical care resource utilisation
articles.take_home: The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is better at predicting which seriously injured trauma patients will need emergency care and blood transfusions than the Shock Index, though both measure similar vital signs. Using NEWS in ambulances could help paramedics identify the sickest patients more accurately.

articles.title: Complications after operatively treated fractures in patients with solid organ transplantation - A systematic review of the literature.
articles.authors: Hubner CT, Anranter A, Kalbas Y, Klingebiel FK, Shehu A, Halvachizadeh S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with solid organ transplants who had operative fracture treatment
articles.sample_size: 2317 patients across 6 studies (range 12 to 2163 patients per study)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications including infection rates, 90-day readmission rates and mortality
articles.take_home: Infection and readmission rates after fracture surgery in transplant patients appear similar to the general population, though mortality varies widely depending on fracture type. More research is needed in this group as studies are currently rare.

articles.title: Investigation of the biomechanically optimal length of intramedullary nails in unstable intertrochanteric femur fractures 31A2.2: A finite element analysis study.
articles.authors: Den S, Ueda K
articles.population: Unstable intertrochanteric femur fractures (AO/OTA 31A2.2)
articles.sample_size: Computer models based on CT data from one average-sized Japanese woman's femur
articles.outcomes: Interfragmentary motion, implant stress, and lag screw stress at different nail lengths (170-280 mm) during simulated stair climbing
articles.take_home: In computer models, using intramedullary nails of 260 mm or longer provided sufficient stability for this type of hip fracture, with motion between fracture fragments levelling off at this length. The nails and screws did not experience stress levels that would cause them to fail under the simulated loading conditions tested.

articles.title: Clinical practice on treatment of primary traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation: a multidisciplinary guideline.
articles.authors: Van Gastel ML, Hekman KMC, Boon F, Nelen SD, Schep NWL, Van der Meijden OAJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients with primary traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation
articles.outcomes: Optimal diagnosis and management pathway including reduction technique, pain management, immobilisation, physical therapy, risk stratification for recurrence, and surgical stabilisation decisions
articles.take_home: Primary anterior shoulder dislocations need prompt imaging and reduction in the emergency department, followed by a week of immobilisation and early physical therapy. Young men and contact athletes have higher risk of the dislocation happening again and may benefit from surgery.

articles.title: Minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis, open reduction and plate fixation, and intramedullary nailing for humeral shaft fractures: A network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Protasio Netto J, Giordano V, Elias N, Belangero WD, Cavalcante B
articles.study_type: Network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults with closed humeral shaft fractures
articles.outcomes: Primary: iatrogenic radial nerve injury. Secondary: nonunion, deep infection, and reoperation
articles.take_home: Minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis (MIPO) appears safer for the radial nerve and requires fewer repeat operations compared to open plate fixation, though the evidence is limited and further research is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: The penetrating injury risk of non-home discharge (PIRD) score: Development and validation of a predictive tool using the National Trauma Data Bank.
articles.authors: Phadke R, Salman S, Ilyas MH, Sontam T, Rana A, Leucht P
articles.study_type: Predictive tool development and internal validation study
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and over with penetrating trauma who survived to discharge
articles.sample_size: 302,399 patients (21,186 with non-home discharge; split 2:1 into derivation and validation sets)
articles.outcomes: Non-home discharge to post-acute care (skilled nursing or inpatient rehabilitation) versus discharge home
articles.take_home: The PIRD score is a new tool that can predict early in a patient's hospital stay whether they will need post-acute care after penetrating trauma rather than going straight home. The score performs better than existing tools and correctly identifies 86% of patients needing post-acute care whilst safely ruling out the need for 98.5% of those predicted to be low risk.

articles.title: Age-stratified outcomes after small-volume isolated blunt traumatic brain injury: A national ACS-TQIP analysis.
articles.authors: Rhodes-Lyons H, McClure DL, Locklear T, Martinek L, Pepe A
articles.population: Adults aged 40 years and older with isolated blunt traumatic brain injury
articles.outcomes: In-hospital mortality and emergency department disposition to intensive care unit
articles.take_home: Older adults aged 65 and over with small-volume brain injuries have significantly higher death rates than younger adults, even when the injuries appear minor on scans. This suggests that age should be considered carefully when deciding on care and monitoring for these patients.

articles.title: A double-hit analysis: Evaluating the nephrotoxicity of dual intravenous and vancomycin impregnated cement exposure.
articles.authors: Vu NH, Esper GW, Egol KA, Ganta A, Konda SR
articles.population: Adults undergoing vancomycin-impregnated cement implantation for fracture-related infection
articles.sample_size: 589 patients (326 receiving intravenous vancomycin plus cement, 263 receiving cement alone)
articles.outcomes: Primary: acute kidney injury incidence; Secondary: changes in serum creatinine levels
articles.take_home: Using intravenous vancomycin alongside vancomycin-impregnated cement did not increase the risk of acute kidney injury compared with cement alone, although it did cause greater rises in creatinine levels. Patients with pre-existing chronic kidney disease had higher rates of kidney injury regardless of which treatment they received.

articles.title: Higher Rate of Treatment Success of Infected Femoral Shaft Non-unions with Ultrathin Silver-Polysiloxane-Coated Implants.
articles.authors: Mueller MM, Niclassen CM, Kowald B, Klinger CE, Gerlach UJ, Grimme C, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with historical control group
articles.population: Patients with infected femoral shaft non-unions
articles.sample_size: 70 patients (8 with silver-polysiloxane-coated implants, 62 with uncoated implants)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: successful treatment at one year (bone healing, full weight-bearing, no recurrent infection). Secondary outcomes: clinical outcomes, blood serum analysis, radiographic outcomes, and patient-reported measures (WOMAC, LEFS, EQ-VAS)
articles.take_home: Patients treated with silver-coated implants had a significantly higher success rate at one year (100% versus 61%) with no safety concerns and lower treatment costs. The coating appears to help prevent recurring infection in this serious bone healing problem.

articles.title: The evolution of primary subtalar arthrodesis for displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures: A historical review.
articles.authors: Schepers T
articles.population: Patients with displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures
articles.outcomes: Union rates, functional outcomes, patient-reported outcomes
articles.take_home: Primary subtalar arthrodesis has evolved over more than a century from a salvage procedure to a selective treatment for severe calcaneal fractures that cannot be reconstructed. Research shows that outcomes depend more on choosing the right patients for this operation rather than the procedure itself.

articles.title: Risk factors and hospital harm: A study of hip fracture patients in the community using population-based data.
articles.authors: Rashidian L, Ali A, Senthinathan A, Bai YQ, Wodchis WP, Bronskill SE, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using linked administrative databases
articles.population: Community-dwelling adults aged 50 and over hospitalized with hip fracture in Ontario, Canada
articles.outcomes: Preventable hospital harm during acute hospital stay for hip fracture
articles.take_home: About 1 in 5 hip fracture patients experienced at least one incident of harm during hospital stay. Men, older patients, those with frailty or dementia, and people in urban areas or undergoing surgery were at higher risk, as were those from neighbourhoods with higher proportions of racialized and newcomer populations.
